items.definition: Navigators or skippers who, together with shipbuilders, developed boats suited to the Tagus's functions and navigation conditions over several centuries.
Naval builders who created boats adapted to transport and fishing and to the differing stretches of the Tagus.
The first of the river's navigational stretches, where conditions differ from the river upstream.
Point marking the end of the stretch running from the estuary; upstream of it begins the next navigational stretch toward Vila Velha de Ródão.
Broad expanse of water in the Tagus estuary at Lisbon, filled with sails of many boat types.
Triangular lateen sails, the usual rig of Tagus boats, whether with one mast or two.
The rigging or sail arrangement of a boat, which varied widely among Tagus vessels.
Carrying capacity of a vessel, which differed greatly between Tagus boat types.
One of the Tagus boat types listed as belonging to the river.
Tagus boats that also ventured out to sea, for example carrying figs to Algarve ports.
A type of Tagus boat listed among the river's vessels.
Boats used for fishing that could also be rigged as a hiate for commercial work.
A type of boat listed among those belonging to the Tagus.
A type of Tagus boat listed among the river's vessels.
A type of vessel; moletas could be rigged as hiates for commercial tasks.
Tagus boats with a single mast carrying a lateen sail.
A type of boat listed among the Tagus vessels.
Small boats listed among Tagus vessels; botes de fragata are also mentioned.
A type of small boat listed among those of the Tagus.
A type of boat listed among those belonging to the Tagus.
Small boats listed among those used on the Tagus.
Name for navigation confined to the river, as opposed to boats that also ventured out to sea.
Boats named as typical of the Tagus, suggesting upstream river navigation.
Boats named among the typical Tagus craft.
A type of boat named among the typical craft of the Tagus.
A type of boat named among the typical craft of the Tagus.
Before the Discoveries, a general term for any small boat used in river traffic or fishing on the Tagus.
Fish-carrying boat designation recorded in the Almada charter of 1190.

numbers.what: year of the Foral de Almada

items.definition: Round sail rig, thought to have been used on the early barcas in voyages directed by Infante D. Henrique.
Lateen sail rig, used on larger vessels such as barinéis and caravels in the Portuguese Discoveries.
Larger vessel type with lateen rig, used after the early barcas in Henrician navigations.
Lateen-rigged vessel that was adapted and improved for difficult long-distance Discovery voyages.
Shallow draught, required for boats going upriver or through the shallow arms of the Tagus.
Hull design with no keel or a half keel, suited to shallow Tagus waters.
items.term: sem quilha ou de meia quilha

items.definition: Type of river boat listed in the 1572 Regimento dos Barqueiros for Tagus traffic; with barcas, served Lisbon.

numbers.what: river boats (barcas and batéis) serving Lisbon in 1552

items.definition: River cargo vessel type listed in the 1572 Regimento dos Barqueiros for Tagus traffic.
Boat first used for carrying goods on the Tagus in the 16th century, later associated with fishing.
Small Tagus river boat type listed in the 1572 Regimento dos Barqueiros.
Towing a boat upstream from the bank, shown in a 1909 image of passing the Cachão do Cabril rapids.
Large ocean-going ships entering Lisbon's port, alongside caravels, from across Christendom.

numbers.what: naus and caravels entering Lisbon port per year, 1552 era

items.definition: Shipyard; each yard or riverside town gave local boats their own style, adding to Tagus boat variety.
Traditional Tagus sailing cargo boat that survived almost to the present day.
Traditional Tagus sailing boat that survived almost to modern times, like the fragata.
Traditional Tagus boat type that once filled the river's waters.
Small traditional boat still kept alive in Sarilhos Pequenos and Moita.
Small traditional Tagus boat, still preserved in Sarilhos Pequenos and Moita.
Type of small Tagus boat once common along the riverside.
Traditional Tagus boat type named among those that once filled the river and estuary.
Boats serving the mills, listed among vanished Tagus craft.
Boat type of the Tagus fragata kind; one example is kept by the Seixal Ecomuseum.
